newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares seen rising over rest of 1997.
newsitem.headline: China B shares seen rising over rest of 1997.

text.p: China's foreign currency B share markets are poised for further rises up to the end of this year despite the recent correction, a research paper by China's top brokerage, Shenyin & Wanguo Securities, said on Tuesday.

The rises will come mainly as a result of China's improving national economic outlook, characterised by high growth and low inflation, along with good performance by B share companies listed since early 1996, the research paper said.

"In the past few days, the B share markets have had an expected correction due to the confirmation of a few market rumours and the pressure of officially orchestrated market adjustments," the paper said.
"But the developing trend of the markets is not in any doubt and the share indices will stabilise," it said. "The key is that investors must have confidence."
The research paper did not predict how high the B share indices would go, but many Chinese analysts believe the indices could hit record highs by the end of the year.
The historical high for Shanghai's B index is 105.78 points set in late 1993. Shenzhen's B index reached 201.87 in late 1996.
From the start of this year to early May, Shanghai's B share index had risen around 50 percent, while its Shenzhen counterpart was up by around 20 percent.

The sharp gains alarmed the securities authorities who took measures to cool the market, including banning state firms from speculative trading. The crackdown has pushed the Shanghai B index down around 20 percent in the past few weeks.
The research paper said the recent powerful correction resulted from prices rising too fast in the first few months of the year.

"In the 14 trading days since April 15, the (Shanghai B index) rose 31 percent, causing an accumulation of huge positions ripe for profit-taking," the paper said. "This caused a five percent plunge on May 8 alone."
But the correction was not strong enough to overwhelm the many positive factors supporting further market rises, the research paper said.

China's gross domestic product rose 9.7 percent in the first three months of this year, with retail price inflation falling to a year-on-year 1.7 percent in March from 1996's 6.1 percent, indicating the economy was developing well, it said.
In addition, a two-year slump on the B share markets before the bull run which started in the second half of 1996 had put the indices at a level that provided huge potential for gains, it said.
By last Friday, the average price earnings ratio of the 43 Shanghai-listed B share firms was 22 times, while that for the 47 Shenzhen-listed firms was 20 times, providing room for further rises.

"Along with the improvement of the macro-economy, the performance of listed firms is expected to improve significantly this year," the research paper said. "Further rises of the B share markets will depend heavily on improved results from listed firms."
On Tuesday, the Shanghai B share index gained 4.41 percent to 85.763 points and the Shenzhen index was up 3.23 percent to 151.07 points.
